cases.oracle: Given a stone cell: click 1 leaves the cell present with crack overlay stage 1 and stone inventory unchanged; click 2 leaves it present with crack stage 2 and stone inventory unchanged; click 3 removes the cell and increments stone inventory by exactly 1 with the HUD count updating. A wood cell behaves identically (present through hits 1-2 with stages 1-2, removed on hit 3, +1 wood inventory).

A single pointer click on a grass cell removes it immediately with no crack stage required and increments grass inventory by exactly 1; a dirt cell behaves the same (one-click removal, +1 dirt inventory).

With inventory[type] = 2, placing that type decrements the count by exactly 1 and writes the cell; with inventory[type] = 0 the placement attempt is refused: the target cell is unchanged and the count stays 0.

After one dig and one place, the single localStorage key holds JSON deep-equal to {version, cells, inventory}; re-initializing from that storage (reload) restores world cells and per-type inventory deep-equal to the pre-reload state; with empty storage the game boots to the default world with an all-zero inventory.

cleanup.environment: Headless node --test run from the repo root; no browser, server, daemon or network connection is started and no environment state persists after the run.
cleanup.data: Tests run against an injected in-memory storage double; real localStorage, user profiles and repo files are never written; any temp fixture lives in a unique tmp directory and is removed in finally.
